The lead's rework verdict on e1a18372 banned a `#[test]` outright when the real requirement was only that no generator write during a default test run. The repository already had an established form for that — six `#[ignore]`d regenerate-twins beside asserting siblings (gate_presets/reference.rs:377, runtime_defaults.rs:127, domain/event_catalog.rs:786, output.rs:3585, storage/reference.rs:786, env-gated schema.rs:1586) — so the verdict created a second convention for one job, which @/invariant/convention-convergence calls a defect. escalations.situation: The plan required ~60 hand-written path literals in the BINARY_BUILD_INPUTS constant plus a reconciliation test against the packaged targets. That is a hand-maintained copy held correct by an assertion — the defect class this container removes — and it ships ~60 of this repository's paths inside every adopter binary. dogfood::jit_dogfood_package() already exposes the parsed embedded manifest and dogfood.rs:386 already filters live assets by the assets/live/ prefix; every live asset's target IS its repository path; and the caller at commands/gate_check.rs:672 sits in a layer that can reach the package.
escalations.resolution: Owner approved rewriting 779ea308 to derive the set from the packaged live-asset targets at the changed-path comparison boundary. REQ-02/REQ-05 (the literals + reconciliation test) replaced; domain-layer purity criterion retained and strengthened.

escalations.category: 4 — issue scope change (criteria) + 1 — new work item
escalations.situation: D-6 requires glob-category exclusions rather than path literals. Measured at execution time: .agents/ is 55 packaged / 52 unpackaged with cleanly categorical exclusions; contrib/ is 1/4; .jit/reference/ is 1/0. But scripts/ is 4 packaged of 45 tracked and no category separates code-review-prompt.md and plan-review-prompt.md (packaged) from doc-review-prompt.md and holistic-review-prompt.md (not), so its exclusion list would be ~41 near-literals and every future unrelated script would fail the walk. Additionally scripts/ai-review.sh and contrib/gates/ai-review.sh are byte-identical and both packaged.
escalations.resolution: Owner approved relocating the four packaged files under contrib/gates/, retiring scripts/ as a declared root, and collapsing the duplicate wrapper. New task 9d451c98 created and wired before 39c34568; 39c34568's REQ-05 no longer fixes a root count.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: `.jit/config.toml:9-49` carries a third hand-maintained copy of the managed/permanent/issue-scoped area lists, asserting at :10-11 that it adopts the shipped classification verbatim with nothing binding it. Surfaced by the 67da1d70 worker.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Out of scope by construction. The plan's 'A residual copy this container does not remove' entry and investigation §4.3 both place it outside REQ-01: it is repository-local policy, not adopter documentation. Re-check at the epic gate against REQ-01's exact wording ('The adopter configuration reference and the copyable example configuration'), which names two documents and does not reach this one.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: CHANGELOG treatment diverged across wave-1 siblings: 67da1d70 added an Unreleased entry for its adopter-visible doc change; 9d451c98 deliberately added none for its adopter-visible packaged-target relocation, reasoning that later issues in this container re-derive the same tree and would rewrite it.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Lead decision: leave both as landed and reconcile the container's CHANGELOG once at epic close, when the packaged tree has its final shape. Both workers' reasoning is defensible; churn now is the worse option. Revisit before the epic's holistic-review gate.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: Every worker running the full `cargo-ci` pipeline itself serialises the whole wave behind the host-wide `flock /tmp/jit-cargo-ci.lock`: four builds queued at once in wave 1, one of them verifying work already rejected in review.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Dispatch-prompt defect on the lead's side. Waves 2-6 instruct workers to run only targeted checks (`cargo test -p jit --lib <module>`, `jit validate`, `docs-mechanical` where cheap); the lead runs the authoritative `cargo-ci` gate once per issue on main after merge.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: `crates/jit/tests/fast_docs_templates/ai_review_verdict_tests.rs:1` carries a `(REQ-11)` tag naming a requirement id local to a different epic (2e926e39). Pre-existing; surfaced by the 9d451c98 worker and left alone.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Outside this container's criteria. Not fixed here; worth a standalone issue at epic close alongside the `jit issue create --description-file` gap.

surfaced_pitfalls.finding: `jit issue create` has no `--description-file` / stdin form, unlike `jit issue update`. Large descriptions must go through `--description "$(cat …)"` and survive shell quoting.

owner_rulings.ruling: No contributed profiles in .jit by default. Our repo shall contain the dogfooding profile, but it shall be disjoint from jit proper. It should be just like an externally contributed profile.
